# Problem 2 - Tidyverse: Tennis

## Load data

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(infer)
```

```{r}
atp_2019_url = paste(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azhou5849/tennis-atp-sackmann-data/",
    "refs/heads/master/atp_matches_2019.csv"
)
if (!dir.exists('p2')) dir.create('p2')
if (!file.exists('./p2/atp_matches_2019.csv'))
    download.file(atp_2019_url, './p2/atp_matches_2019.csv')
```

```{r}
atp_2019 <- read.csv('./p2/atp_matches_2019.csv')
```



## Process data

a. How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
atp_2019 %>% summarize(tourney_count = n_distinct(tourney_id))
```



There are 128 tournaments took place in 2019.


b. Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
atp_2019 %>%
    filter(round == "F") %>%
    group_by(winner_id, winner_name) %>%
    summarize(win_count = n_distinct(tourney_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(win_count > 1) %>%
    arrange(desc(win_count))
```



There are 12 players who won more than one tournament. The most winning players are Novak Djokovic and Dominic Thiem, who both won 5 tournaments.


c. Is there any evidence that winners have more aces than losers? (If you address this with a hypothesis test, do not use base R functionality - continue to remain in the Tidyverse.)

```{r}
atp_2019 %>%
    select(w_ace, l_ace) %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    mutate(ace_diff = w_ace - l_ace) %>%
    summarise(
        n = n(),
        mean_diff = mean(ace_diff),
        se = sd(ace_diff) / sqrt(n),
        t_stat = mean_diff / se,
        p_value = pt(t_stat, df = n - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
    )
```



Since p < 0.001, there is strong evidence that winners have more aces than losers on average.


d. Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. (Note that this is NOT asking for the highest number of wins.) Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
bind_rows(
    atp_2019 %>%
        select(winner_id, winner_name) %>%
        mutate(
            id = winner_id,
            name = winner_name,
            win = TRUE
        ) %>%
        select(id, name, win),
    atp_2019 %>%
        select(loser_id, loser_name) %>%
        mutate(
            id = loser_id,
            name = loser_name,
            win = FALSE
        ) %>%
        select(id, name, win)
) %>%
    group_by(id, name) %>%
    summarise(total_game = n(), win_rate = mean(win), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(total_game >= 5) %>%
    arrange(desc(win_rate)) %>%
    mutate(win_rate = round(win_rate, 4)) %>%
    slice_head(n = 5)
    
```



Rafael Nadal has the highest win-rate with 86.96% after attending 69 matches.
